survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA in Focus synthesis uses PISA 2018 financial literacy results across participating OECD countries and partner economies, based on the OECD PISA 2018 Database. The document reports descriptive comparisons (e.g., mean scores, proficiency-level distributions, and adjusted score gaps after accounting for mathematics/reading and student characteristics), which in PISA are typically produced using the study’s complex-sample design weights. The PISA in Focus text does not specify the exact weight variable names or whether replicate-weight variance estimation was used, so analysts should apply the standard PISA student sampling weights and replicate procedures provided in the OECD PISA database when reproducing estimates. No machine-learning model training is described here; therefore, weighting is relevant for population-representative inference and for correct standard errors rather than for ML algorithm fitting.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA in Focus brief summarizes PISA 2018 financial literacy results for 15-year-old students across 13 OECD countries/economies and 7 partner countries/economies (about 117,000 students, representing around 13.5 million students). It reports cross-country differences in mean financial literacy scores and the distribution of proficiency levels (e.g., Estonia highest; OECD average comparisons; Level 5 top performers and Level 1-or-below low performers). The brief also describes within-country and subgroup patterns: gender gaps (boys higher overall but over-represented at both ends), socioeconomic gradients (advantaged students higher by about one proficiency level), and immigrant-background differences after accounting for socioeconomic status. It further links financial literacy to related skills measured in mathematics and reading (about 80% of score variation reflects skills also measured there) and to learning/exposure channels (parental information, school exposure to financial literacy tasks, and use of financial products). The document is descriptive and policy-oriented; it does not provide an explicit ML modeling framework or performance metrics for predictive algorithms.
